body.p: Applicant submits this Amendment and Response to address the final Office Action dated July 1, 2024 ("Office Action"). Claims 5 and 18-20 were previously cancelled. Claims 9-17 were previously withdrawn. Claims 1-4, 6-17, and 21-23 are pending. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application as amended.
Upon allowance of claim 1, Applicant respectfully requests rejoinder of withdrawn claims 9-17 at least because claim 9 includes features similar to those recited in claim 1.

Applicant thanks the Examiner for granting the interview conducted on September 25, 2024. During the interview, the parties discussed a proposal aimed at overcoming the 101 and 103 rejections of the independent claims. The Examiner suggested a tweak to the proposed claim and thought that formal submission of claim amendments that mirrored those discussed would likely be sufficient to overcome the rejections. Accordingly, Applicant submits the instant response with claim amendments that reflect those presented and discussed during the interview and intended to overcome the 101 and 103 rejections.

Claims 1-4, 6-8, and 21-23 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 for being directed to non- statutory subject matter. Applicant has amended the independent claims in accordance with the proposal discussed during the interview and the modification suggested by the Examiner for overcoming the 101 rejection. For at least this reason, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection.

Claims 1, 2, 7, 8, and 21-23 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over International Patent Publication No. 2020/072335 to Nikou et al. ("Nikou") in view of U.S. Publication No. 2019/0321657 to Hale ("Hale").
Claims 3 and 4 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over Nikou in view of Hale, and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2014/0206990 to Epstein et al. ("Epstein").
Claim 6 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being obvious over Nikou in view of Hale in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2019/0090955 to Singh et al. ("Singh").

To establish aprimafacie case of obviousness, all claim limitations must first be taught or suggested by the prior art. See, e.g., DyStar Textilfarben GmbH & Co. Deutschland KG v. C.H. Patrick Co., 464 F.3d 1356, 1360 (Fed. Cir. 2006); 80 U.S.P.Q.2d 1641, 1645 (2006). "All

words in a claim must be considered in judging the patentability of that claim against the prior art." MPEP § 2143.03 (citing In re Wilson, 424 F.2d 1382, 1385, 165 USPQ 494, 496 (CCPA 1970)). The Examiner must then provide an explicit analysis of the motivation for combining the references. See KSR Int'l Co. v. Teleflex Inc., 550 U.S. 398, 418 (2007); 82 U.S.P.Q.2d 1385, 1396 (2007) ("a patent composed of several elements is not proved obvious merely by demonstrating that each of its elements was, independently, known in the prior art . . .."). While the Examiner can choose one of several exemplary rationales from the MPEP to support an obviousness rejection, all the rationales in the MPEP still require the Examiner to demonstrate that all the claim elements are taught or suggested in the prior art. See MPEP §2143.
Without conceding to the Examiner's position, Applicant has amended claim 1 in
accordance with the proposal discussed during the interview. Applicant submits that the cited art does not disclose or suggest claim 1 for at least the same reasons discussed during the interview.

For example, the cited art does not disclose or suggest steps of registering "a patient to a pre-operative image to yield a correlation between a coordinate system associated with the patient and a coordinate system associated with a navigation system, wherein the correlation is used to track the robotic arm relative to the anatomical element," and reregistering "the patient to the pre-operative image based on the notification indicating that the relative pose of the first tracking device and the second tracking device has changed, wherein reregistering the patient to the pre-operative image yields an updated correlation between the coordinate system associated with the patient and the coordinate system associated with the navigation system," and then using "the updated correlation to automatically position the robotic arm relative to the anatomical element," in combination with the other features of claim 1. Paragraph 53 of Nikou is relied upon to teach the previously recited registering and reregistering steps and teaches that a

robotic arm may be controlled by computer-assisted surgical system (CASS) in accordance with a pre-operative or intraoperative surgical plan. However, this is not specific enough to disclose or suggest registering "a patient to a pre-operative image to yield a correlation between a coordinate system associated with the patient and a coordinate system associated with a navigation system, wherein the correlation is used to track the robotic arm relative to the anatomical element," and reregistering "the patient to the pre-operative image based on the notification indicating that the relative pose of the first tracking device and the second tracking device has changed, wherein reregistering the patient to the pre-operative image yields an updated correlation between the coordinate system associated with the patient and the coordinate system associated with the navigation system," as recited in claim 1. Moreover, the remainder of Nikou appears silent with respect to registration and reregistration steps as claimed, especially when considered in combination with the other features of claim 1.

The other cited references have not been relied upon to remedy the deficiencies of Nikou and do not appear to do so. Accordingly, claim 1 and its associated dependent claims are patentable over the cited art. Claim 21 recites features similar to those discussed above with respect to claim 1. Thus, claim 21 and its associated dependent claims are patentable over the cited art for at least the same reasons as those discussed above with respect to claim 1.

Based upon the foregoing, Applicant believes that all pending claims are in condition for allowance and such disposition is respectfully requested. Applicant does not acquiesce to any objection, rejection, or argument not specifically addressed herein. Rather, Applicant believes the amendments and arguments contained herein overcome all objections, rejections, or arguments. In the event that a telephone conversation would further prosecution and/or expedite allowance, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned.
